ALL-ORDER RESPONSE OF A COLLECTIVELY SLOW INTERACTING CHAIN
1 November 2026

Main finding

The interaction-word barrier is removed for a concrete nonlinear kinetic-Ising
family. The full magnetization response, including every interaction order,
has an explicit randomized algorithm with expected arithmetic cost

  O_b(n log n delta^-2 log(1/eta))

before integer precision factors. Delta is requested relative error and eta
the failure probability. The model has correlation length proportional to n
and collective relaxation time proportional to n^2. The operation uses no
2^n-state probability vector and does not simulate all physical spin events.

This is a scoped mathematical and executable advance. It is not yet a general
theory for interacting matter, and historical novelty has not been established.
The strongest conventional constructions remain part of the result: some are
substantially faster at moderate accuracy. The meaningful acquired step is an
all-order work/variance bound, not a claim to invent positive duality or
importance sampling.

Exact scope

The physical chain has zero field, periodic boundary, uniform microscopic
clocks, ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor equilibrium, and rates

 w_i=(1-b sigma_(i-1)sigma_(i+1))/2
       *[1-gamma sigma_i(sigma_(i-1)+sigma_(i+1))/2],
 gamma=tanh(2J), 0<b<1/2, gamma(1-b)>b.

The modification acts at every site and preserves the common Gibbs equilibrium.
Its rate contrast is fixed, (1+b)/(1-b). The executed collective sequence is
b=1/3 and exp(2J)=n. All rate and equilibrium inputs used computationally are
rational: t=(n-1)/(n+1), gamma=(n^2-1)/(n^2+1).

The observable is chi=<M,K^+M>=integral Cov(M(0),M(t))dt, M=sum sigma_i.
Var(M)=Theta(n^2) and chi/Var(M)=Theta(n^2). Thus the observable carries the
collective slow dynamics. Fields, arbitrary local kinetic modifications,
conservation and higher-dimensional lattices are outside this theorem.

What was constructed

The exact action of the nonlinear target generator on odd spin products is
a positive process of hopping, branching and pair annihilation, with killing
kappa N, kappa=(1-b)(1-gamma). All odd particle counts remain present. The
packed triple is the exact local departure state when a singleton branches;
it is not a retained three-defect sector.

LOCAL CONDITIONAL-SCHUR RESPONSE CONSTRUCTION
Independent interacting-system contribution, 1 November 2026

Status
------
This contribution combines the root's local bounded-overlap coupling estimate
with a positive-semidefinite Schur-complement refinement and a complete recursive
implementation. It is an explicit response construction for a separated hierarchy
of genuinely interacting Gibbs chains. Conditional averaging and Schur complements
are conventional machinery. No priority, arbitrary-clock uniform complexity, or
general superiority over strong conventional multiscale solvers is claimed.

1. A real obstruction to naive physical-support localization
---------------------------------------------------------
Take a free-boundary zero-field Ising chain sigma_0,...,sigma_L with homogeneous
J>0, t=tanh J, and ordinary heat-bath rates. Site 0 has clock epsilon; every other
site has clock one. Equilibrium is independent of the clocks. For f=sigma_L,

    Cov(f,sigma_0)=t^L,
    <sigma_0,K sigma_0>_pi=epsilon(1-t^2).

The variational Poisson principle therefore gives

    chi_f >= t^(2L)/[epsilon(1-t^2)].

Choosing epsilon=t^(4L) makes this lower bound grow exponentially with distance,
although equilibrium correlations decay exponentially and the microscopic rates
are an ordinary fixed local heat-bath rule. A fixed-radius physical neighborhood
around f misses the response-dominating remote spin. Spatial mixing alone is not
a clock-independent relative-response localization theorem.

The missing source projection is exactly acquired here:

    E[f | sigma_0]=t^L sigma_0.

Its slow averaged rate is epsilon(1-t^2); the displayed lower bound is the exact
response of that acquired conditional projection under the averaged slow chain.
A rate-ordered innovation basis might help encode such projections, but no
clock-uniform comparison or locality theorem for that general proposal has been
proved in this contribution. Do not substitute it as a finished primitive.

2. Exact conditional decomposition
----------------------------------
Work in L2(pi), where K=-L is the nonnegative self-adjoint generator. Let P be
conditional expectation given a selected set of slow spins, Q=I-P. Write

    K=K_F+K_S,

where K_F consists of fast updates and K_S of slow updates. Conditional fast
equilibration is exact: ker K_F=range P. On Q let F=K_F|Q>0. Define

CONDITIONAL AVERAGING: STRONG CONVENTIONAL FINITE-RESPONSE COMPARISON
Date: 2026-11-01

Outcome
-------
An equally informed conventional construction -- conditional averaging,
conditional product Poincare, two-coloring, variational bounds and ordinary PSD
Schur algebra -- acquires essentially the same complete finite-accuracy scalar
response as the proposed local-monomial construction on the collective test.
This does not establish that one cited paper or package already implements the
whole combination. It demonstrates that the available conventional ingredients
are constructive, including the accuracy bound, on the same microscopic input.

1. Exact reduction shared by both constructions

In L2(pi), split fast and slow flips, K=KF+KS, with P conditional expectation
given slow spins, Q=I-P. Let F=KF|Q, A=PKSP, B=QKSP, C=QKSQ.
Then K has block matrix [[A,B*],[B,F+C]], and KS>=0 implies
  C>=B A^+ B*.
For f=p+q, p=Pf, put a=<p,A^+p>, b=<q,F^-1q>.
If B*F^-1B<=theta A, eliminating A first gives
  chi=a+<q-B A^+p,(F+C-B A^+B*)^-1(q-B A^+p)>.
Since the inverse is bounded above by F^-1,
  a<=chi<=(1+theta)a+b+2sqrt(theta a b).
This is a direct block variational/Schur-complement bound, valid for alltheta>=0.
It is tight given only a,b,theta: take scalar A,F with C=B A^-1 B* and choose
the relative source sign to maximize the cross term.

The slow chain A is exactly the ordinary conditional averaged chain. Checkerboard
decimation of a nearest-neighbor Gibbs chain preserves nearest-neighbor Gibbs
potentials, including fields. Its averaged slow flips depend on only three
retained spins. A pair-additive source remains pair-additive, since the
conditional mean of a removed binary spin is an arbitrary function of its two
retained neighbors, hence a linear combination of1,sL,sR,sLsR. The residual
source is a sum of independent centered fast spins with acquired conditional
coefficients. Therefore b is a finite local sum. These closure facts apply to
the conventional construction as well.

2. Dimension-free coupling from elementary coloring

At a fixed slow configuration y, the fast spins are independent, and
  B u=sum_i [r_i-E_F r_i] Delta_i u.
Each residual rate depends on the two neighboring fast spins. The dependency
graph of slow rate residuals is a path; color its vertices with two colors.
Within a color, centered rate residuals are independent and orthogonal.
